'''Andreas Wallraff''' is a German [[physicist]] who conducts research in [[quantum information processing]] and [[quantum optics]]. He has taught as a professor at [[ETH Zürich|ETH Zurich]] in [[Zürich, Switzerland|Zurich, Switzerland]] since 2006.<ref name="QuDevSite">{{cite web |url=https://qudev.ethz.ch/andreas_wallraff |title=Quantum Device Lab |date= |access-date=2017-06-03 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160519235222/http://qudev.ethz.ch/andreas_wallraff |archive-date=2016-05-19 |url-status=dead }}</ref> He worked as a research scientist with [[Robert J. Schoelkopf]] at [[Yale University]] from 2002 to 2005, during which time he performed experiments in which the coherent interaction of a single photon with a single quantum electronic circuit was observed for the first time.<ref name="Nature2004">A. Wallraff, D. I. Schuster, A. Blais, L. Frunzio, R.- S. Huang, J. Majer, S. Kumar, S. M. Girvin, and R. J. Schoelkopf, "Strong coupling of a single photon to a superconducting qubit using circuit quantum electrodynamics", ''[[Nature (journal)|Nature]]'' '''431''', 162-167 (2004), {{doi|10.1038/nature02851}}</ref> His current work at ETH Zurich focuses on hybrid quantum systems combining [[superconducting]] [[electronic circuits]] with [[semiconductor]] [[quantum dots]] and individual [[Rydberg atoms]] as well as [[quantum error correction]] with [[superconducting qubits]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.qudev.ethz.ch/research%20topics |title=Quantum Device Lab Research Topics |date= |access-date=2017-06-19 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170813221633/https://www.qudev.ethz.ch/research%20topics |archive-date=2017-08-13 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

He has contributed primarily to the field of [[quantum information science]], particularly in [[superconducting quantum computing]] and hybrid quantum systems.<ref name="Tagesanzeiger2011">{{cite news|url=http://www.tagesanzeiger.ch/digital/computer/Auf-dem-Weg-zum-Schweizer-Supercomputer/story/25692897 |title=Auf dem Weg zum Schweizer Supercomputer |newspaper=Tages-Anzeiger |date=2011-06-28 |access-date=2017-06-03}}</ref>

== Education and earlier work==
Andreas Wallraff obtained his undergraduate degrees in physics from [[Imperial College London]] and [[RWTH Aachen University]] and conducted research  on [[soliton]] dynamics in stacked [[superconductor-insulator-superconductor tunnel junction|Josephson tunnel junctions]] for his master's degree at the [[Forschungszentrum Jülich]] and RWTH Aachen, which he earned in 1997.<ref name="QuDevSite" /><ref>{{cite web |url=http://qudev.phys.ethz.ch/content/science/thesis/dipl_wallraff.pdf |title=Fluxon Dynamics and Radiation Emission in Twofold Long Josephson Junction Stacks |date=1997-01-27 |access-date=2017-06-15 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161107062056/http://qudev.phys.ethz.ch/content/science/thesis/dipl_wallraff.pdf |archive-date=2016-11-07 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref name="FIRSTprofile">{{cite web|url=http://www.first.ethz.ch/people/people-a-z/person-detail.html?persid=134453 |title=Wallraff, Andreas, Prof. Dr. |date= |access-date=2017-07-06}}</ref> During his doctoral research on soliton and vortex  dynamics in superconductors at the [[University of Erlangen-Nuremberg]], he observed for the first time the tunneling and energy level quantization of an individual [[quantum vortex]] for which he obtained a PhD degree in physics in 2000.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://qudev.ethz.ch/content/science/thesis/dr_wallraff.pdf |title=Fluxon Dynamics in Annular Josephson Junctions: From Relativistic Strings to Quantum Particles |date=2000-07-18 |access-date=2017-06-15 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070720041233/http://qudev.ethz.ch/content/science/thesis/dr_wallraff.pdf |archive-date=2007-07-20 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Following his doctoral research, Wallraff continued to work as a research scientist and later as an assistant professor at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg.<ref name="FIRSTprofile" /> In 2002, he left Europe to work as a postdoctoral researcher with Robert J. Schoelkopf within the Department of Applied Physics at Yale University in [[New Haven, Connecticut]].<ref name="FIRSTprofile" /> During this time, he was an author on papers regarding the coupling of superconducting [[qubits]] via a [[microwave cavity|cavity]] [[Quantum bus|bus]] and the coherent interaction of a single photon to a [[Cooper-pair box]], among others.<ref name="Nature2004" /><ref>J. Majer, [[J. M. Chow]], J. M. Gambetta, J. Koch, B. R. Johnson, J. A. Schreier, L. Frunzio, D. I. Schuster, A. A. Houck, A. Wallraff, A. Blais, [[M. H. Devoret]], S. M. Girvin, and R. J. Schoelkopf, "Coupling superconducting qubits via a cavity bus", ''Nature'' '''449''', 443-447 (2007), {{doi|10.1038/nature06184}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.photonics.com/Article.aspx?AID=30972|title=All Aboard the Quantum 'Bus'|access-date=2017-08-07|date=2007-09-27}}</ref> In 2004 he was appointed as an associate research scientist in the Department of Applied Physics at Yale and in June 2005 he was elected as a tenure-track assistant professor at ETH Zurich.<ref name="FIRSTprofile" /> Following the professorship appointment, he departed from Yale and started the Quantum Device Lab at ETH Zurich in January 2006.<ref name="Tagesanzeiger2011" /> In 2011, he was chosen from among 380 ETH Zurich professors to be awarded the [[:de:Max Rössler|Max Rössler]] Prize for his research activities.<ref name="Tagesanzeiger2011" /> In 2012, he worked as a visiting professor at the [[Kastler-Brossel Laboratory]] within the [[École Normale Supérieure]] in [[Paris, France]].<ref name="QuDevSite" />

== Research topics ==
Wallraff has in recent years been studying a variety of topics related to quantum information science. Among them include interactions between distant [[Circuit quantum electrodynamics#Artificial atoms.2C Qubits|artificial atoms]],<ref>A. F. van Loo, A. Fedorov, K. Lalumière, B. C. Sanders, A. Blais, and Andreas Wallraff, "Photon-Mediated Interactions Between Distant Artificial Atoms", ''[[Science (journal)|Science]]'' '''342''', 6165, 1494-96 (2013), {{doi|10.1126/science.1244324}}</ref> quantum [[many-body]] systems,<ref>C. Eichler, J. Mlynek, J. Butscher, P. Kurpiers, K. Hammerer, T. J. Osborne, and A. Wallraff, "Exploring Interacting Quantum Many-Body Systems by Experimentally Creating Continuous Matrix Product States in Superconducting Circuits", ''[[Physical Review X]]'' '''5''', 041044 (2015), {{doi|10.1103/PhysRevX.5.041044}}</ref> digital [[quantum simulation]],<ref>Y. Salathé, M. Mondal, M. Oppliger, J. Heinsoo, P. Kurpiers, A. Potočnik, A. Mezzacapo, U. Las Heras, L. Lamata, E. Solano, S. Filipp, and A. Wallraff, "Digital Quantum Simulation of Spin Models with Circuit Quantum Electrodynamics", ''Physical Review X'' '''5''', 021027 (2015), {{doi|10.1103/PhysRevX.5.021027}}</ref> [[quantum nonlocality]],<ref>M. Jerger, Y. Reshitnyk, M. Oppliger, A. Potočnik, M. Mondal, A. Wallraff, K. Goodenough, S. Wehner, K. Juliusson, N. K. Langford, and A. Fedorov, "Contextuality without nonlocality in a superconducting quantum system", ''[[Nature Communications]]'' '''7''', 12390 (2016), {{doi|10.1038/ncomms12930|doi-access=free}}</ref> the implementation of the [[Toffoli gate]] in quantum computation,<ref>A. Fedorov, L. Steffen, M. Baur, M. P. da Silva, and A. Wallraff, "Implementation of a Toffoli gate with superconducting circuits", ''Nature'' '''481''', 170-172 (2012), {{doi|10.1038/nature10713}}</ref> [[Determinism#Quantum mechanics and classical physics|deterministic]] [[quantum teleportation]],<ref>L. Steffen, Y. Salathe, M. Oppliger, P. Kurpiers, M. Baur,	C. Lang, C. Eichler, G. Puebla-Hellmann, A. Fedorov and A. Wallraff, "Deterministic quantum teleportation with feed-forward in a solid state system", ''Nature'' '''500''', 319-322 (2013), {{doi|10.1038/nature12422}}</ref><ref name="NatGeo2013">{{cite web|url=http://news.nationalgeographic.com/news/2013/08/130814-physics-quantum-computing-teleportation-star-trek-qubit-science/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130815013655/http://news.nationalgeographic.com/news/2013/08/130814-physics-quantum-computing-teleportation-star-trek-qubit-science/ |url-status=dead |archive-date=August 15, 2013 |title=Teleportation: Behind the Science of Quantum Computing |date=2013-08-14 |access-date=2017-07-06}}</ref> and the [[Hong-Ou-Mandel effect]].<ref>C. Lang, C. Eichler, L. Steffen, J. M. Fink, M. J. Woolley, A. Blais, and A. Wallraff, "Correlations, indistinguishability and entanglement in Hong–Ou–Mandel experiments at microwave frequencies", ''[[Nature Physics]]'' '''9''', 345-348 (2013), {{doi|10.1038/nphys2612}}</ref> [[File:4 Qubit Chip, 10.1103.PhysRevX.5.021027 (A. Wallraff, 2015).png|thumb|A [[integrated circuit|chip]] with four superconducting [[transmon]] qubits made by Andreas Wallraff and colleagues. Two of the qubits were used in the experiment which led to the publication of [https://journals.aps.org/prx/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevX.5.021027 "Digital Quantum Simulation of Spin Models with Circuit Quantum Electrodynamics"] in [[Physical Review X]] in June 2015.|left]]

In general, his research is primarily focused on investigating [[circuit QED]] (cQED) systems and their applications in [[superconducting quantum computing]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.qudev.ethz.ch/research%20topics |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170813221633/https://www.qudev.ethz.ch/research%20topics |url-status=dead |archive-date=2017-08-13 |title=Research Topics |date= |access-date=2017-06-22}}</ref> These include implementing [[quantum gates]], identifying and eliminating sources of [[quantum decoherence]] to extend [[Relaxation (NMR)#T1 and T2|qubit lifetimes]], and creating [[Solid-state electronics|solid-state]] architectures in which [[quantum error correction]] is possible.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.qudev.ethz.ch/research_topics/quantum_information_processing |title=Quantum Information Processing |date= |access-date=2017-06-22}}</ref> In addition, he conducts research into "hybrid quantum systems"; cQED systems interacting with [[Rydberg atoms]] and [[semiconductor]] [[quantum dots]] to combine "the long coherence times available in microscopic quantum systems with the strong interactions and integration available in solid state systems... [to allow] for strong interactions with control fields and thus fast manipulation of the [[quantum state]] of a system."<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.qudev.ethz.ch/research_topics/hybrid_quantum_systems |title=Hybrid Quantum Systems |date= |access-date=2017-06-22 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170813224717/https://www.qudev.ethz.ch/research_topics/hybrid_quantum_systems |archive-date=2017-08-13 |url-status=dead }}</ref> His research has been honoured with multiple awards, such as the ETH Zurich's [[Rössler Prize|Rössler-Prize]] in 2013<ref>{{Cite web |title=Rössler Prize • ETH Zürich Foundation |url=https://ethz-foundation.ch/en/roessler-prize/ |access-date=2024-11-01 |website=ETH Zürich Foundation |language=en-US}}</ref> and the [[Helmholtz International Fellow Award]] in 2020.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2020-11-13 |title=Andreas Wallraff receives Helmholtz International Fellow Award 2020 |url=https://ethz.ch/en/the-eth-zurich/portrait/latest-honours-and-prizes/2020/11/wallfraff-helmholtz-international-fellow-award.html |access-date=2024-11-01 |website=ETH Zurich |language=en}}</ref>  [[File:Double Quantum Dot, 10.1103.PhysRevX.7.011030 (A. Wallraff, 2017).png|thumb|"A gate-defined [[GaAs]] double [[quantum dot]] (DQD) and a frequency-tunable [[high impedance]] [[resonator]] realized using an array of [[superconducting quantum interference devices]]... [This] false-color optical micrograph of a representative device [indicates] the substrate (dark gray), the superconducting structures (light gray), the gold top gates (yellow) forming the DQD, and its source and drain leads and contacts (blue)."<ref>A. Stockklauser, P. Scarlino, J. V. Koski, S. Gasparinetti, C. K. Andersen, C. Reichl, W. Wegscheider, T. Ihn, K. Ensslin, and A. Wallraff, "Strong Coupling Cavity QED with Gate-Defined Double Quantum Dots Enabled by a High Impedance Resonator", ''Physical Review X'' '''7''', 011030 (2017), {{doi|10.1103/PhysRevX.7.011030}}</ref>|right]]

== Positions and speaking engagements ==
Since January 2006, Wallraff has held a professorship position at ETH Zurich where he is the head of the Quantum Device Lab within the Laboratory for Solid State Physics.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.solid.phys.ethz.ch/people/person-detail.html?persid=134453 |title=Wallraff, Andreas, Prof. Dr. |date= |access-date=2017-06-03}}</ref> He has been awarded several grants, including two from the [[European Research Council]] (one in 2009 for hybrid [[cavity quantum electrodynamics]] and one in 2013 for superconducting [[quantum networks]])<ref>{{cite web|url=https://erc.europa.eu/projects-figures/erc-funded-projects/results?search_api_views_fulltext=andreas+wallraff |title=ERC Funded Projects |date= |access-date=2017-06-03}}</ref> and holds positions as the President of the Strategy Commission for the Department of Physics and Deputy Head of the Laboratory for Solid State Physics at ETH Zurich.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.phys.ethz.ch/the-department/management.html |title=Department Management and Administration |date= |access-date=2017-06-03}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bi.id.ethz.ch/personensuche/personenDetail.view?page=1&lang=en&schnellSuche=andreas+wallraff&order=NAME&descending=false&paging=true&pid=20d35 |title=Andreas Wallraff |date= |access-date=2017-06-03}}</ref> He is also a member of the Scientific Committee for the [[Swiss National Science Foundation]] National Center of Competence in Research (NCCR) in Quantum Science and Technology (QSIT),<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.snf.ch/SiteCollectionDocuments/nfs/nccr_guide_2017.pdf |title=National Centres of Competence in Research |page=52 |date= |access-date=2017-06-03}}</ref> a member of the Global Future Council for the Future of Computing at the [[World Economic Forum]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.weforum.org/communities/the-future-of-computing |title=The Future of Computing |date= |access-date=2017-06-03}}</ref> and an Associate Fellow of the [[Canadian Institute for Advanced Research]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.cifar.ca/profiles/andreas-wallraff/ |title=CIFAR |date= |access-date=2017-06-03 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160817114605/https://www.cifar.ca/profiles/andreas-wallraff/ |archive-date=2016-08-17 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Wallraff has been an invited speaker at several talks and conferences, including at the inaugural celebration for the Center for Quantum Coherence Science at the [[University of California, Berkeley]],<ref>{{cite web |url=http://live-cqcs.pantheon.berkeley.edu/fiqcs/program/ |title=Center for Quantum Coherent Science |date=2017-01-09 |access-date=2017-06-03 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170826144102/http://live-cqcs.pantheon.berkeley.edu/fiqcs/program/ |archive-date=2017-08-26 |url-status=dead }}</ref> [[The Optical Society]] "Quantum Information and Measurement - Quantum Technologies" meeting at the [[Pierre and Marie Curie University]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.osa.org/en-us/meetings/topical_meetings/quantum_information_and_measurement_(qim)_-_iv_qu/invited_speakers/ |title=OSA Quantum Information and Measurement |date= |access-date=2017-06-20}}</ref> the IWQD 2017 workshop at the [[National Institute of Informatics]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://home.hiroshima-u.ac.jp/mhirokaw/iwqd/iwqd2017/program.html |title=IWQD 2017 |date= |access-date=2017-06-20}}</ref> and the 635th WE [[Heraeus]] Seminar<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.zurich.ibm.com/heraeus/program_tues.html |title=IBM 635th WE-Heraeus Seminar |date=2017-01-31 |access-date=2017-06-03}}</ref> in 2017. In 2016 he spoke at the [[Institute of Physics]] Silicon Quantum Information Processing meeting at [[Murray Edwards College, Cambridge]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://siqip2016.iopconfs.org/speakers |title=IOP Silicon Quantum Information Processing 2016 |date=2017-01-31 |access-date=2017-06-03}}</ref> the [[University of Science and Technology of China]],<ref>{{cite web |url=http://quantum.ustc.edu.cn/icqft/uploads/ICQFT2016_Program6.pdf |title=The International Conference on Quantum Foundation and Technology |date=2016-11-16 |access-date=2017-06-03 }}{{Dead link|date=June 2020 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> and the SCALEQIT International Conference at the [[Delft University of Technology]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.chalmers.se/SiteCollectionDocuments/Mikroteknologi%20och%20Nanovetenskap/ScaleQIT.pdf |title=Delft SCALEQIT 2016 |date= |access-date=2017-06-20}}</ref>

In previous years he also spoke at the [[University of Oxford]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cs.ox.ac.uk/qisw2012/program.html |title=QISW 2012 Workshop Program |date=2012-03-30 |access-date=2017-06-03}}</ref> the [[Max Planck Institute for the Science of Light]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.mpl.mpg.de/en/institute/news/news/article/mpl-distinguished-lecturer-series-prof-andreas-wallraff.html |title=MPL Distinguished Lecturer Series |date=2014-05-08 |access-date=2017-06-03}}</ref> the Institute for Theoretical Atomic Molecular and Optical Physics (ITAMP) 2015 workshop at [[Harvard University]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cfa.harvard.edu/itamp-event/light-matter-interactions-low-dimensions |title=Light Matter Interactions in Low Dimensions |date=2015-06-29 |access-date=2017-06-03}}</ref> and the [[Kavli Institute for Theoretical Physics]] at the [[University of California, Santa Barbara]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://online.kitp.ucsb.edu/online/denselight_c15/ |title=Non-equilibrium Dynamics of Strongly Interacting Photons |date=2015-10-07 |access-date=2017-06-03}}</ref>
